subject: Your personal skills.sh map — Marcus asked me to send this
body:
GD — FR here, Research Lead on Forge. Marcus asked me to send each agent a personalized skills.sh map. Here is yours.

YOUR DOMAIN FINGERPRINT:
You own the Detroit Pistons visual language: #C8102E red, #1D42BA blue, #002D62 navy, #BEC0C2 chrome. You write the voice guide. You design for a 15-year-old with ADHD — Kai. Every design decision in MCM must account for attention, short text, clear hierarchy, visible progress, and one action at a time. This is not generic ed-tech design. It is specific, personal, and constrained. That constraint is your superpower.

YOUR TOP 10 FROM SKILLS.SH:

1. web-design-guidelines — 115,700 installs (highest on the platform in your domain)
   Why: Comprehensive web design standards. Even in a brand-constrained system like Detroit Pistons, formal design guidelines fill in the gaps your brand guide does not cover — accessibility, responsive behavior, interaction states.

2. frontend-design — anthropics — 86,000 installs
   Why: Core frontend design patterns. Component architecture, layout systems, design-to-implementation handoff patterns. Directly applicable to how you hand off specs to GA.

3. ui-ux-pro-max — nextlevelbuilder — 33,000 installs
   Why: Advanced UI/UX patterns. Interaction design, micro-animations, state transitions. For an ADHD user like Kai, micro-interaction design is especially important — progress indicators, feedback states, attention cues.

4. canvas-design — anthropics — 9,500 installs
   Why: MCM uses Chart.js for performance visualization. You should be designing those charts, not just leaving them to GA with default styling. This skill covers canvas-based visualization design.

5. tailwind-design-system — wshobson/agents — 9,300 installs
   Why: Design system methodology. You do not use Tailwind, but this skill covers design token architecture, component naming conventions, and systematic visual consistency — all applicable to the MCM design system you own.

6. brand-guidelines — anthropics — 6,900 installs (estimated install count)
   Why: You own the Detroit Pistons brand application. Formal brand guidelines methodology covers how to document and enforce brand consistency across multiple templates and contributors.

7. design-md — google-labs-code/stitch-skills — 7,300 installs
   Why: Design documentation format for AI agent consumption. Directly applicable to how you write design specs that GA will implement. Structured spec intent reduces implementation mismatches.

8. interface-design — dammyjay93 — 4,800 installs
   Why: Interface design patterns with focus on interaction behavior. For ADHD-specific design (Kai), interaction patterns — button states, navigation, focus management — matter as much as visual design.

9. copywriting — 17,400 installs
   Why: You own the voice guide. Marcus's coaching voice is specific and disciplined. Copywriting frameworks (problem-agitation-solution, direct voice) help you capture and document that voice consistently.

10. copy-editing — 9,600 installs
    Why: You review student-facing content across all exam files. Copy editing methodology — editing for clarity, brevity, and tone — is a distinct skill from writing and directly applicable to your review work.

BEYOND SKILLS.SH (where skills.sh is thin for your domain):
- Microsoft Inclusive Design (microsoft.com/design/inclusive): ADHD is explicitly covered. The Inclusive Design Toolkit has patterns specifically for attention and cognitive load. This is required reading for Kai's UX and not covered anywhere on skills.sh.
- WCAG 2.2 AA (w3.org/WAI/WCAG22): Accessibility standards that apply to student-facing tools. Focus management, color contrast ratios (the Detroit Pistons palette needs to be verified against contrast requirements), keyboard navigation.
- Detroit Pistons brand history (NBA.com and team archives): The visual identity has evolved since 1957. Understanding the history gives you authority when you make brand interpretation decisions for Marcus.

START HERE: web-design-guidelines (highest install, broadest coverage) and Microsoft Inclusive Design (ADHD-specific, directly relevant to Kai). Those two fill your biggest gaps.

FR — Research Lead, Forge
